specification_compliance: R4-1 (I8) is addressed. TranscriptEditDialog.tsx:72-78 adds a mountedRef that is set to false when the dialog unmounts. save (102-130) calls onSaved only while mounted (115), returns from catch before onChanged or setError once unmounted (117), and guards setSaving in finally (129). The fileId effect (TranscriptSection.tsx:332-343) clears editTarget, so the old dialog unmounts before a new one can open. Opening the new one needs a tap on a strip 修正, so there is always a render with editTarget null between them. That makes the new dialog a fresh instance with its own mountedRef, and the old save's closure only ever reads the old, now-false ref. The late answer can no longer call closeEditDialog/setEditTarget(null), focusRow, refreshAfterWrite or setActionError on the new file.

A reload does not unmount the dialog: loading is set only on a first load for a fileId (TranscriptSection.tsx:347-348), and `if (loading || !hasAnything) return null` (1043) therefore runs only on a file change or when every source is empty. So the guard does not swallow the answer of a save that is still on screen during a WS or refresh reload (F6/I8 hold).

The new jsdom tests (TranscriptSectionTouch.test.tsx, 'keeps the next file's dialog and draft when the previous file's save answers … late', for a success and for `changed`) would fail without the guard. On success, onSaved → closeEditDialog → setEditTarget(null) would close the next file's dialog. On `changed`, it would also write CHANGED_MESSAGE. Both assertions catch that.

I1-I7, I9-I11: the fix commit touches nothing outside the dialog's post-await path, so the r4 trace of these still applies. The strip is gated on isSelected, which requires coarse. The fine controls are gated on !coarse. The dialog sends expected_text/expected_start captured at open. `saving` blocks save, close and Escape, and the field is readOnly while saving.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A dialog save that succeeds after its dialog has unmounted now triggers no refreshAfterWrite. For a file change this does not matter, because the panel loads the new file. The spec does not say whether a save that completes after an automatic source switch should still reload. A WS transcript.updated event would normally reload anyway.
regression_risks: The inline (fine-path) saveEdit (TranscriptSection.tsx:968-1016) still writes setEditingIndex/setActionError/refreshAfterWrite after its await with no file or mount guard. It can still close a newly opened inline editor or report the old file's `changed` message on the next file. This is pre-existing and unchanged here; I9 requires the fine path to behave as before.

If every source becomes empty while the dialog has a save in flight, the early `return null` (TranscriptSection.tsx:1043) unmounts the dialog without clearing editTarget. With the new guard the late success no longer clears editTarget either, so the dialog would reappear from the stored target once a source becomes available again. The last_utterance check makes reaching this unlikely.
The `if (mountedRef.current) setSaving(false)` guard in finally is not pinned by any test, because React ignores a state update on an unmounted component. Removing it changes nothing visible.
test_coverage: TranscriptSectionTouch.test.tsx now covers a late success and a late `changed` from the previous file's save while the next file's dialog has a typed draft. It asserts that the dialog, the draft and an empty panel error line survive.

Mutation in thought: drop `if (mountedRef.current)` before onSaved at TranscriptEditDialog.tsx:115. The success case is killed because the next dialog closes. Drop the `return` at 117. The `changed` case is killed because the dialog closes and CHANGED_MESSAGE appears. Drop the finally guard at 129. That mutant survives, but it is harmless.
No test covers a late answer after an automatic source switch, or after the all-sources-empty unmount.
No test asserts where focus goes when the dialog closes (B10). This is unchanged since r2.

trajectory: The only change since r4 is 08b6c6304, an addon bump. It adds one state: a mountedRef in TranscriptEditDialog, with three guards after the save's await. It also adds two jsdom tests for a late answer. The round before, 884a57bb3, added a prediction (a clamp) to revealCue's upward scroll, and r3's 3da286167 added a `!following` condition to the reveal effect. This round's guard sits in a different component and on a different concern, the lifetime of an async save, so it does not repeat what the previous round added. Each round since r2 has added one guard that answers the previous review's finding, so the change is growing one guard per round. Still, no two consecutive rounds add to the same branch, state or prediction, so the design is not being patched on one point. No round removed a branch or a state.
